title: Hang a 4-ft LED wrap light on its four ceiling screws with a partner robot, then tighten the two at your end
instruction: With the robot across from you, hang the light on the four screws in the ceiling by its keyholes: lift it off its stands, keep it level, move it toward its pencil outline until the round centres of its four keyholes are under the screw heads, raise it against the ceiling, slide it on into its outline so each screw goes into a keyhole's narrow slot, lower it onto the heads and let go. Then, with the screwdrivers beside you, tighten the two screws at your end until your end is held tight against the ceiling.

context: Electricians (821,000 in the US, O*NET 47-2111.00) install fixtures as core work. This light's maker recommends two people and the keyhole method: "install the four wood screws (AA) ... leaving a 3/8 in. gap", "Guide the heads ... into the keyhole slots", "Slide the fixture (A) until the wood screws (AA) are secured into the narrow ends of the keyhole slots", "Tighten the wood screws (AA) until the fixture is secured in place." Each robot is one of the two people, at one end of the bare 1.2 m housing, and the two cannot talk. The task tests blind overhead engagement of four screw heads, hidden above the back, through keyholes with about 0.75 mm to spare all round; agreeing on the slide (both ends raised together with their keyholes over the heads, then slid together into the outline); letting go only once it hangs; then each robot tightening its own two screws overhead with a push-to-start screwdriver. Neither can reach the far end. The light is never powered.
setup: Millimetres; origin midway between the two stations; x from station A toward station B, y to A's left, heights above the table top. Two bimanual YAM stations face each other across the table, 1,308 apart: A's arms at x -654, y +305 (left) and -305 (right), facing +x; B's at x +654, its left at y -305 and right at +305, facing -x. Ceiling stand-in: a 23/32 in (18 mm) plywood panel 1,400 x 600, x -700 to +700, y -300 to +300, its underside 760 above the table, stiffened by two 2x4 rails on edge along its top over the long edges, on four 2x4 legs at x +/-120, flush against its long edges (y +/-319), each screwed to the panel's edge and its rail and standing on a 150 x 150 plywood foot clamped to the table. A pencil outline on its underside marks the light's place: ends at x +/-609, long sides at y +/-160. Four #8 x 3/4 in pan-head square-drive wood screws are driven into the panel before the trial, at x -403 (A's end) and +423 (B's end), y +/-95, each in a 50 mm plug of the panel's own plywood (a 1/8 in pilot hole at its centre; the plug sits in a 2 in hole, glued to a 100 mm cap screwed to the panel's top). Each head is left 3/8 in (9.5) below the ceiling, set with a 3/8 in spacer, as the maker's guide says. Light: a Commercial Electric WR484080LSL 4-ft LED wrap light (Home Depot 313512347; 47.96 x 14.13 x 2.82 in and 10.4 lb with its lens), lens and channel cover off as in the maker's step 1. Bare steel housing (estimate: 1,218 x 320 x 55, 3.7 kg), back up, open side down, long axis along x, on two stands (2x4 posts at x +/-300, y 0, with 400 mm 2x4 crossbars across it, padded with 10 mm foam), its back 30 below the ceiling and its centre at x +15, y 0: 15 toward B of its outline. Its back has four keyholes, about 826 apart along it and 190 across (centres at x +/-413, y +/-95 from its middle), each a round centre hole (3/8 in, 9.5) with a narrow slot (3/16 in, 4.8) running 12.5 each way along the light (sizes estimated from the maker's drawing; the real slots decide). Hung in its outline, each screw sits in the B-side narrow slot, 10 from its centre hole. Push-on rubber edge trim (8 across, 24 tall, 80 long) covers the long walls' lower edges at the four grip spots, 80 in from each end. Screwdrivers: four Bosch GO (Gen 3) push-to-start cordless screwdrivers (3.6 V, 306-396 rpm), one beside each arm, each with its clutch at the lowest setting (or the lowest that seats a screw: pre-trial check) and a #2 square bit, standing bit up on a holder: a 4x4 (89 x 89) riser on a clamped plywood base topped with a 22 mm square hardwood peg, 30 tall, its top 350 above the table. In each station's own frame (x forward from its arms, y to their left) the holders are at (120, +450) and (120, -450), each peg turned 60 degrees outward from straight ahead so its faces are square to the hand's approach. The robots use each GO in push-to-start mode: the motor runs while the bit is pressed against a screw and stops when the push is released (the on/off button is not used). Nothing else is on the table. The light is never connected to power.
scoring: Scored on the end state, except that a drop at any time scores 0. Dropped: at any time an end of the light comes down 10 mm or more onto a stand, the table, the floor or a robot while no gripper holds that end (closed on it, the light not slipping) and it is not on its screws (video; sim: the same, from contact sensors on the stands, table, floor and every arm link, the grippers' opening and slip, and the keyhole geometry). Hung on a screw: its shank is in a narrow slot of its keyhole (either one), clear of the round centre hole, with the back above the head (look up into the open housing; sim: the shank at least 6.85 mm along the slot from the hole's centre and the head under the back). Tight, each screw: (1) seated: a 0.5 mm feeler blade does not go between its head and the back; (2) flush: a 2 mm shim pushed flat against the ceiling at the long edge nearest the screw, in line with it, does not go in; (3) clamped, both screws of an end together: a 25 N pull (up to 30 N if the pre-trial calibration needs it) across the light at that end (luggage scale on a cord loop round a long wall's lower edge, 100 mm from the end, each way) moves it less than 0.1 mm on a dial indicator (an unclamped end turns about the far end within the shank's play; a clamped end is held by friction at the heads and the ceiling; 25 N outweighs a far end clamped as hard as the demo's); sim: head within 0.3 mm of the back, clamping it with 50 N or more, and that edge within 2 mm of the ceiling. Hangs on its own: for the last 3 s no robot touches the light: no link of any arm and no screwdriver in a hand (video; sim: contact sensors on every arm link and on the screwdrivers). 1.0: hung on all four screws, all four tight, and it hangs on its own. 0.75: hung on all four, hangs on its own, both screws of one end tight, not all four. 0.5: hung on all four, hangs on its own, no end's two screws tight. 0.25: not dropped and hung on at least one screw, but less than 0.5 (one end hung only, or a robot still touches it in the last 3 s). 0: dropped at any time, or hung on no screw. A run the spotter stops is scored on its state at the stop. Real trial, right after the run, in this order: the video for a drop and for the last 3 s; look up into the housing at each keyhole; the 2 mm shim at each screw's nearest edge; the 0.5 mm blade under each head; the 25 N pull at each end whose screws passed, each way.
reset_notes: Support the light by hand; back each screw out about five turns, slide the light 10 mm toward B so the heads are in the centre holes, and lower it onto its stands, 15 mm toward B of its outline (marks on the crossbars). Set each screw's 3/8 in gap with the slotted spacer: turn the screw until its head just touches the spacer, then remove it. Stand each screwdriver on its holder's peg. Rest the arms 10 min or more; start when every coil reads 50 °C or less (T_Rotor). Replace a plug when its screw spins without drawing up (about every 20 trials, estimate).
fidelity: Rigid PhysX, 240 Hz. Each screw's z joint follows its spin (1.69 mm/turn). Head collider: a non-turning 8 x 4.2 mm block, +/-2.65 mm of play along the slot in the 9.5 mm hole (real round head +/-0.75 mm). Task code drives the bit contact, push-to-start motor (3 N) and clutch (0.6 N m). Tight: 50 N clamp. Touch: any arm link or held driver; drop: onto supports, non-gripper links or loose drivers, with no gripper closed on that end without slip. Estimated: housing, keyholes, torques, push.
scores: Dream-1, one session per robot (dream_pair): 0 (6,000 steps = 300 s; neither robot touched the light; camera frames checked clean every 500 steps); scripted demo, one controller per robot: 1.0 in 1,342 steps (3 identical runs)
